content: The global :focus-visible rule sets `border-radius: var(--r-sm)` on every element that gains keyboard focus. Because the property is applied to the element itself (not the outline), it mutates the element's actual border-radius — any element without an explicit radius will snap from 0 → 8px on focus and back on blur (visible jank on native <button>/<select>/<a>), and elements with custom radii (e.g., pill-shaped `.nm-tag` at 9999px) will be overridden while focus is visible. Remove the border-radius from this rule so the outline shape follows each element's own radius in modern browsers; if a uniform focus shape is desired, scope it to a specific selector rather than every focused element.

**`useDropdownTop`: ResizeObserver setup race when refs are null at first effect run.** The branch is gated on `(rootRef.current || btnRef.current)`, so if neither ref has been populated yet (forwarded refs to lazily/conditionally mounted children, portal targets, etc.) the observer is skipped and only `window.resize` is subscribed. Because the dep array tracks ref *identity* rather than `.current`, and React does not re-run effects when `.current` mutates, the observer is never retroactively installed once the refs eventually populate. Subsequent button/root size changes (icon swap, async font load, width jitter — exactly what the comment promises to handle) will leave `top` stale until the window is resized. The fallback was meant only for environments without ResizeObserver, but the condition conflates the two cases.

**`useOutsideClose`: no keyboard handler — Escape does not dismiss the dropdown.** The hook only binds `mousedown` on `document`. For a popover/menu driven by a button trigger, dismissing on `Escape` (and ideally `focusout` / `Tab` moving focus outside) is the standard keyboard-accessibility expectation (WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices for menu/menubutton). Keyboard-only users currently have no way to close the dropdown except by `Tab`-cycling focus away — and even that doesn't fire `mousedown`, so the dropdown stays open. This is a regression in `useOutsideClose`'s contract: its name implies "outside" rather than specifically "outside click".

Prototype-chain safety: `LOBE_ICONS` and `PROVIDER_ALIASES` are plain `Record` objects that inherit from `Object.prototype`, so lookup with vendor names like `constructor`, `toString`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty`, `__proto__`, etc. resolves to the inherited function/object instead of `undefined`. `slugIcon` is declared `string | null`, but `slugIcon("constructor")` actually returns the inherited `Function` constructor. Downstream code that uses the result as a URL (e.g. ``) will receive a non-string and break at runtime. Use `Object.create(null)` or `Map` for both tables (and add an own-property guard inside `slugIcon` / `resolveLobeIcon`).

Pure-function contract violated: header states "纯函数，无 React/DOM 依赖（单测锚点）", but `toGraphologyGraph` defaults `now = Date.now()`. Layout (and `nodeSize` for `doing` tasks) becomes non-deterministic between calls, breaking snapshot-style unit tests and any retry/regenerate path that should be idempotent. Recommend requiring `now` as a parameter (or accepting it as `number` with no default) so the caller controls the clock — `GraphPage` already knows when it's building the graph.

Semantic mismatch between sector placement and anchor wiring. `groupOfNode` assigns each node to the FIRST matching tag group (`break` on first hit), so the node is positioned inside that group's sector. The later `membersByGroup` pass, however, walks every tag and registers the node under EVERY group it touches — so the same node receives `TAG_EDGE_WEIGHT` star edges to anchors of groups whose sector it does NOT occupy. Under FA2 these cross-sector anchors will pull nodes out of their intended sector, contradicting the documented "同标签（同义组）节点铺在专属扇区内" invariant. Either unify to one traversal with a single rule (e.g. first-match wins, consistent with sector placement), or document the intentional many-anchor behavior and adjust the initial placement to match.

loadAnchor only validates that x/y are finite numbers and that edge is in the allow-list — it does not bound-check x/y against the current screen. A saved anchor from a now-disconnected second monitor, or coordinates left in storage by an older build, will restore a widget that is permanently off-screen with no UI to drag it back. Pair the loader with a clamp against screenSize() (or a similar guard) before returning the Anchor.

`draftFromDecompose` performs an unchecked array access: `nodes[d].localId` will throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` whenever an AI/server response breaks the "d < 自身下标" guarantee (e.g. out-of-range index, duplicate index, negative number). A malformed LLM payload would crash canvas load. Add a runtime guard (skip / log / fall back) and/or validate `s.dependsOn.every((d) => d >= 0 && d < nodes.length)` before mapping.

The cache defaults to 7 days and `applyArchiveRule` reads it synchronously, but the JSDoc only says the async load "should" be called before the first rule application — nothing here prevents a caller from invoking the rule before the awaited `loadArchiveDaysFromConfig()` resolves, in which case tasks are archived against the wrong threshold. Consider gating the first render behind an explicit "not yet loaded" state, or exposing a ready promise the UI must await.

For done tasks missing `completedAt`, the function falls back to `now` and returns a clone carrying that timestamp. The clone is only useful if the caller persists it back; otherwise each call recomputes `now`, so the task appears to have been "just completed" forever and can never cross the `afterMs` threshold — legacy done tasks will be stuck in the 完成 column. Either require a real `completedAt` from the data source, persist the fallback, or treat tasks without a known completion time as already-archivable / ineligible with explicit semantics.

All three IPC functions use a bare `catch {}` that silently discards the original error. When the Rust module panics or the IPC channel fails, there is no log line, no console warning, and no preserved error object — the documented "null = meta 模块异常" path is completely opaque to developers and to users. At minimum, log the error (`console.error` / `logger.warn`) so that an environment without the Rust backend (or with a broken one) is diagnosable. This violates the async-handling rule about meaningful error reporting.

`NotificationItem.payload` is declared `Record<string, unknown> | null`, but the surrounding `kind` field is a discriminated union (`memory_proposal | evolution_proposal | artifact_bind | workflow_question`). Any consumer that reads `payload` for a specific `kind` will be working with `unknown` and can crash at runtime with a null/undefined property access (violates the null-check rule). Either (a) model `payload` as a discriminated union keyed by `kind` (e.g., `MemoryProposalPayload | EvolutionProposalPayload | … | null`) so TypeScript narrows it automatically, or (b) export per-kind payload interfaces plus a runtime guard helper so callers can't access fields without narrowing first.

TypeScript type <-> Rust serde drift risk: every row/detail type is hand-mirrored from `src-tauri/src/db/trace.rs` with no runtime validation. If a Rust field is renamed, removed, or its nullability changes, `invoke<T>` will silently mis-shape (e.g. `traceDetail(...).spans` could be `undefined` while the type asserts an array) and downstream code will throw at use sites rather than at the boundary. Consider adding a shared schema (zod / valibot) parsed at the IPC boundary, or at minimum an `assertShape` dev-only check, so the contract is enforced and the failure surfaces next to `trace.ts`.

content: The `default` field is documented as a red line invariant ('必非空' = must be non-empty) but the type allows `string | null`. This type/contract drift means callers cannot rely on a non-null default at compile time, and if the backend ever returns null, it will silently violate the documented invariant. Either tighten the type to `string` and have the backend omit the field when there is no assumption, or document explicitly that `null` means "no assumption available" and downgrade the comment.

content: `respondWorkflowQuestion` does not validate the (action, answer) pair before invoking the IPC command. `action` is only a compile-time union, so runtime calls can send `answer: null` when the user picked "answer", or send an arbitrary `answer` alongside "assume"/"dismiss". The comment states answer/assume/dismiss have distinct semantics, but the wrapper silently normalizes invalid inputs via `answer ?? null` instead of throwing or surfacing a clear error. Add a precondition check (e.g. require non-blank `answer` for action "answer" and disallow `answer` for the other two actions).

Stale-closure hazard: `handler` is intentionally excluded from the effect dependencies, so the listener keeps invoking whatever closure was captured on first mount. Any caller that passes a non-stable callback (the typical React pattern) will process events with stale props/state. Either document this contract loudly at every call site, store `handler` in a ref updated on every render and call `ref.current(e.payload)`, or use React 19's `useEffectEvent` so the dependency array can stay `[event]` without freezing the callback.

Post-cleanup event delivery race: `cancelled` is only checked when storing the resolved unlisten function, not before invoking `handler(e.payload)`. `listen` registers the native listener before its promise resolves, and `unlistenSafe` only kicks off the async unlisten. An event arriving between (a) registration + cleanup-set-cancelled, or (b) cleanup + actual native unlisten, will still reach the handler with no guard, potentially firing setState on an unmounted component or running side effects after teardown. Add an `if (cancelled) return;` (or a `mountedRef.current` check) inside the listener callback.
existing_code: listen<T>(event, (e) => handler(e.payload))

content: Setter accepts and persists arbitrary-length values despite the exported MAX_GUIDANCE_CHARS (2000) limit. If callers do not validate independently, the UI may report "已保存" while the backend (Rust MAX_GUIDANCE_CHARS) silently rejects the oversized guidance on the next decompose invocation, leaving stale storage out of sync with what the user sees. Either validate `v.length <= MAX_GUIDANCE_CHARS` here (and report failure) or document the caller-side contract.

Inconsistent error handling between read and write paths. `loadProfile` routes failures through `handleCommandError(..., { silent: true })` and rethrows, but `setProfileName`, `setProfileAvatar`, and `removeProfileAvatar` have no `.catch()` at all — failed writes surface as raw rejections to the caller and skip the shared UI error prompt the read path relies on. Either route write errors through `handleCommandError` (matching `loadProfile`) or document why the write path deliberately leaves reporting to its callers.

`profile-changed` listener writes `cache = e.payload` directly without consulting `loadGen`, so it bypasses the generation protocol used everywhere else. Combined with `adoptProfile`'s gen check, a write whose response resolves AFTER another writer's broadcast event (e.g. concurrent edits from a different window/挂件) can still satisfy `gen === loadGen` and overwrite newer state with its own response. Either gate the event handler by `loadGen` (and increment before applying, or skip when not the latest local op) or drop the gen check in `adoptProfile` — the two mechanisms are not currently consistent.

Cross-webview state divergence: each Tauri webview has its own isolated localStorage, so `emit()` only broadcasts the change event — it does NOT write the new value into other webviews' localStorage. A widget opened after the main window set the flag to `true` will still read `false` from its own localStorage. The "self-heal on reload" comment is incorrect: reloading the widget re-reads the SAME webview's localStorage, not a synced value. Subscribers that re-read localStorage on the event will still get the wrong (default) value. Consider also persisting the value through a Tauri-side store / command, or having each webview initialize its localStorage from a shared source on startup.

STORAGE_KEY literal is "***" — the comment above says this is the legacy localStorage key consumed by first-run migration. As shipped, `localStorage.getItem("***")` will always return null, so every existing user's prior data will be silently discarded during migration. This is a clear placeholder that was never filled in (or was meant to be filled by a code generator). Either replace with the real key or remove the constant + its export if migration is already complete.
suggestion_code: export const STORAGE_KEY = "<actual-legacy-key>";
existing_code: export const STORAGE_KEY = "***";

content: Path regex can over‑match: the space‑allowing branch (`PATH_CHAR_SPACE*?` … known extension) has no left token boundary and permits spaces and most ASCII punctuation, so a token can start inside a larger word (e.g. `foo/home/user/a.pdf`) and the space‑allowing branch can swallow ordinary prose until a later whitelisted extension. This can still produce the “Program”/wrong‑path problem the comment claims to fix. Consider adding a left boundary (look‑behind or explicit preceding whitespace/start) and constraining `PATH_CHAR_SPACE` so it cannot run across sentence punctuation.

URL branch keeps Markdown link delimiters such as a trailing `)` or `]`. The capture group excludes `< > " '` and full‑width punctuation but not ASCII parentheses/brackets, while `normalizeUrl` only strips `[.,;:!?]+$`. As a result `[label](https://example.com)` yields the URL `https://example.com)` which is opened verbatim. Either extend the URL character class to exclude trailing `)]` (or a balanced pair) or have the normalizer strip the closing bracket/parenthesis when it follows an URL scheme.

Native prototype mutation lacks a runtime guard. The function deliberately mutates `Element.prototype` — which the project's own security rules prohibit — and is exported with no check that it is being called from a jsdom test suite. `src/test/setup.ts` shows the project deliberately keeps setup.ts free of global prototype patches and pushes them into per-suite helpers like this one, so the risk is bounded today, but if a non-test file ever imports `stubScrollNoop` (e.g. a refactor that pulls a shared util into `src/`), the patch becomes permanent for the whole process. Suggestion: assert at the top of the function, e.g. `if (typeof window === "undefined" || typeof Element === "undefined") return;` or `if (process.env.NODE_ENV === "production") return;`, so accidental production use becomes a no-op rather than a silent global mutation.

localStorage shim implements only length/clear/getItem/key/removeItem/setItem but is typed as the full Storage interface (forEach, keys(), values(), entries(), [Symbol.iterator] are required by current lib.dom). Any production code that iterates storage (e.g., for...of over `localStorage`, `localStorage.forEach`, `localStorage.keys()`) will throw `TypeError: ... is not a function` at test time, producing silent test-coverage gaps. Add the missing methods (entries/keys/values returning IterableIterator via the same store, a forEach that delegates, and a [Symbol.iterator] that yields entries()).

`cancelledRef` is only cleared by a later blur or an explicit commit, but the documented contract lets `onCancel` simply set `editing` false (no blur is guaranteed when React unmounts the focused input). In that case the flag stays true across edit sessions: the next `editing` false→true transition resets the draft and `committedRef`, but `cancelledRef` is still true, so the first real blur of the new edit is treated as the leftover cancellation and `onBlur` returns without committing — the user's edit is silently dropped. Reset `cancelledRef` whenever a new edit session starts (mirror the `committedRef` reset) and, if the input can stay mounted, also when a new user-driven draft change occurs so an Escape stays scoped to the focus that triggered it.

Enter handler calls send() regardless of viewedBusy, but the UI affordance (send button replaced by stop button) suggests sending should be blocked during an in-flight reply. Add a viewedBusy guard so keyboard and button stay consistent.

`displayTask` does not force-open a card whose `collapsed` is `undefined` when targeted by `editingId`. The outer (non-editing) branch explicitly maps `undefined → collapsed: true`, which implies `TodoCard` treats `undefined` as folded by default. For a pinned-jump target whose `collapsed` is `undefined`, the function returns `t` unchanged, so the card stays folded and `autoEdit` puts the title into edit mode behind a collapsed body — the user can't see the edit field, defeating the whole purpose of the forced-open behavior described in the comment. Treat `undefined` the same as `true` when `editingId` matches and force it to `collapsed: false`.
suggestion_code:
const displayTask = (t: Task): Task =>
    t.id === editingId
      ? t.collapsed === false
        ? t
        : { ...t, collapsed: false }
      : t.collapsed !== undefined
        ? t
        : { ...t, collapsed: true };
existing_code:
const displayTask = (t: Task): Task =>
    t.id === editingId
      ? t.collapsed === true
        ? { ...t, collapsed: false }
        : t
      : t.collapsed !== undefined
        ? t
        : { ...t, collapsed: true };

Clicking flips `open`, but `open && children` keeps the panel out of the DOM, so the control is effectively dead — users see a caret toggle that does nothing. Either hide/disable the button when `!children`, or always render an empty panel placeholder so the state stays consistent with the UI.

content: Race condition: after `setSessionId(rest[0].id)` and `await bot_history_load`, the code unconditionally calls `setMessages(rowsToMsgs(rows))` without the `sessionIdRef.current === sid` guard that `switchSession`/`openExecSession` use. If the user switches to another session during the await, the freshly-loaded history from `rest[0]` will be rendered into the now-current view. Mirror the existing pattern: capture the target sid, then guard the `setMessages` (and the new-session branch) on `sessionIdRef.current === targetSid`.

Mount-time init does `setSessionId(cur.id)` but never synchronously mirrors to `sessionIdRef.current`, unlike `switchSession`/`openExecSession` which set both together. Until the next render fires the `useEffect([sessionId])` mirror, any `bot-chat-delta`/`bot-tool`/`bot-usage-delta` arriving for the freshly-loaded session will be filtered out by `sessionIdRef.current !== sid` and the start of the assistant's reply can be lost (initial mount is exactly when history is fresh and any in-flight streamed continuation lands here).

Trailing punctuation stripping silently drops visible text and can corrupt valid URL/path endings. The regex `/[.,;:!?]+$/` removes terminal `.`, `,`, `;`, `:`, `!`, `?` and the stripped suffix is never re-rendered as a plain span, so sentences like `Visit https://example.com.` lose the period. It also mangles legitimate endings such as URLs whose query string ends with `!`/`?`/`:` (e.g. `https://x/?q=!`) or a filesystem path whose name legitimately ends in punctuation (e.g. `C:\archive.`). Preserve the stripped suffix as plain text and/or only strip punctuation that is provably not part of the URL/path.

content: Regex recognition is purely a presentation classifier, not a security boundary. `isHttpUrl` only toggles `href`/`role`/`tabIndex`, while `openTarget(clean)` is invoked unconditionally for every matched token. If `openTarget` shells out (e.g. Electron `shell.openExternal` / `shell.openPath`), it must independently allowlist HTTP(S) schemes, reject dangerous schemes (e.g. `javascript:`, `file:` outside the intended paths, `mailto:`), and contain filesystem paths. Verify the helper enforces scheme allowlisting and safe path handling rather than relying on this component.

The dropdown declares `role="menu"` with multiple `role="menuitem"` children, but the only keyboard handling here is `Escape`. Per the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices, a menu widget must support `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` (and typically `Home`/`End`) to move focus between menuitems, and `Tab` to close. Without this, keyboard-only users can open the menu but cannot move between sessions, which is a real a11y regression. Consider adding a `useRef`-tracked active index + onKeyDown handler on the container that focuses the next/prev menuitem button via `.focus()` (and calls `e.preventDefault()`).

The per-row Trash2 button calls `onDelete(s.id)` directly on click with no local guard. Combined with the small `w-5 h-5` click target sitting flush next to the wide session title button, a misclick (mouse jitter, touch tap on the wrong row, accidental `Enter` while focus is on the delete button) will permanently destroy a conversation with no confirm and no undo. Either (a) wrap the click with a `window.confirm`/inline confirm step locally, (b) gate deletion behind a two-step interaction (first click arms, second click confirms within a short window), or (c) ensure the parent `onDelete` always shows a confirm dialog — and at minimum stop `e.stopPropagation()` so the click doesn't also bubble and trigger the session-select handler if the parent ever nests them.

                className="shrink-0 w-5 h-5 flex items-center justify-center rounded text-[var(--t5)] hover:text-[var(--danger)] hover:bg-[var(--hover-bg)]"
                title="删除此对话"
                onClick={(e) => {

                    onDelete(s.id);
                  }
                }}
              >

              </button>

content: Silent error swallowing in respond() — invoke failures are caught and only `console.error`-ed, but the modal is unconditionally cleared in the `finally` (`setPending(p => p === cur ? null : p)`). When `bot_confirm_response` fails, the user sees their click "succeed" (modal closes, buttons re-enable) and believes the dangerous action was confirmed/denied, when in fact the backend never received the decision. The header comment claims backend timeout is the fail-safe, but for an in-flight failure the modal is already gone so the user has no way to retry or be warned. Surface the error to the user (toast, inline error, or keep modal open on failure) so the decision isn't silently dropped.

`proposal.related_refs.length` is read without a null/undefined guard. If `related_refs` is optional in `ProposalEntry` (or arrives undefined at runtime for any reason), the dialog throws on first render and never reaches the user. Guard with optional chaining and treat absent refs as `0` so the UI degrades to the non-cascade option rather than crashing.

```ts
const refsCount = proposal.related_refs?.length ?? 0;
```

All three dismissal paths (Cancel button, Escape key, backdrop click) are gated on `!busy`, and the Cancel button is `disabled={busy}`. If the parent's async delete throws and never clears `busy`, the user is permanently locked inside this modal with no recovery. There is no timeout, no force-close, and no error-aware dismissal. Either (a) keep dismissal always enabled and let the parent's `onCancel`/`onConfirm` be a no-op while `busy`, or (b) have the parent mount a watchdog/finally that resets `busy` even on error.

```tsx
onClick={onCancel}  // never disabled
```

**Evidence record key/lookup mismatch**: The record is keyed by `e.proposalId` (camelCase), but `ProposalCard` looks it up by `p.proposal_id` (snake_case, matching `ProposalEntry`'s convention used everywhere else in this file). If `ProposalEvidence` actually has a snake_case `proposal_id` field like the other domain types, every lookup returns `undefined` and the conflict/shadow-verdict UI never renders — silently broken. Verify against `./types` and either key by `e.proposal_id` or look up by `p.proposalId` for consistency.

**Evidence lookup uses snake_case key that may not match**: Consistent with the keying concern above — `evidence[p.proposal_id]` reads via snake_case while the map was built via `proposalId`. If `ProposalEntry.proposal_id` and `ProposalEvidence.proposalId` resolve to the same string value (only the field name differs), this still works by accident; if they truly differ as field names, every lookup fails. Confirm naming in `./types` and unify.

content: Concurrency: `reloadTasks` and `applyRemoteRows` directly mutate `tasksRef.current` and call `setTasks` outside the module-scope `mutating.chain`, re-introducing the SYNC-1 race that TP-1/TP-3 tied everything to the chain for. If a `tasks-updated` widget event or a user-initiated `mutate` is mid-flight on the chain, these bypasses can race (e.g., `reloadTasks` reads DB, chain writes `next` into `tasksRef`, then `reloadTasks` overwrites with stale DB state, losing the chain's write). Route both through `mutating.chain` (e.g., wrap in `mutating.chain = mutating.chain.then(() => …)` or expose a `mutateDbReload` helper).

Concurrency: `applyRemoteRows` mutates `tasksRef.current` and `setTasks` directly, bypassing `mutating.chain`. Called after `task_set_column` / `task_patch` invocations complete; if a `tasks-updated` widget event for the same row arrives concurrently, the chain will process it first then `applyRemoteRows` overwrites with a potentially stale row. Route through the chain for ordering consistency.

`commitBoardOrder`'s failure-recovery path calls `reloadTasks().catch(() => {})`. Because `reloadTasks` bypasses the chain (see related issue), this is a race: an optimistic UI write is set synchronously, an invoke fails, the catch silently swallows reload errors AND races with any in-flight `tasks-updated` handler. Additionally, if BOTH `task_set_column` and `task_reorder` fire and only one fails, `reloadTasks` reverts the successful change too. At minimum, log the reload failure; ideally make failure recovery idempotent on the chain.

Accessibility — missing `aria-controls` linkage to the panel being toggled. The button advertises `aria-expanded`, but screen readers have no way to associate the toggle with the region it expands/collapses. Add an optional `controlsId?: string` prop that, when provided, is forwarded as `aria-controls={controlsId}`; consumers (TodoCard/TaskCardContent) should pass the id of the content region they wrap. Without this, the expand/collapse relationship is invisible to assistive tech and fails WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).

content: `handleDragEnd` mixes two state sources in a way that is subtle and easy to break. The early-return branch (over null / self-over) commits the live `draft` snapshot to capture cross-column moves done during `dragOver`, while the main branch recomputes from the original `tasks` prop via `spliceMove(tasks, ...)`. If a reviewer later changes the main branch to use `draft` (or vice versa), intra-column reorders will start losing intermediate cross-column hops, or the cross-column path will stop firing when `over` is the column container. Worth a comment block at the top of `handleDragEnd` explaining the invariant: "if `over` is a valid drop target we trust `spliceMove(tasks, ...)` because it knows the final rect; otherwise we fall back to whatever `draft` accumulated."

content: Stale list after all running rows finish: the 10 s polling is gated on `hasRunning`, and the page never listens for backend trace events. If the page is opened while no trace is running, the initial `trace_list` snapshot never refreshes — any new execution started later (manual / chat / scheduled / workflow) will not appear until the component is remounted or a previously‑running trace happens to flip `hasRunning` true. That defeats the page's "最近全部执行痕迹" purpose. Either keep polling unconditionally at a low cadence while the page is mounted, or subscribe to a backend event (e.g. extend `trace_sink::begin_trace` / finish hooks with `app.emit`) and reload on it, with the interval kept only as a safety net.

Camera animation state is corrupted by drag and never restored. On every `pointermove` during drag, `sigma.getCamera().animated = false` is set to suppress pan, but `onUp` only resumes FA2 and resets cursor — `animated` is never set back to `true`. Any later `sigma.getCamera().animate(...)` (e.g. `fitToContent` on theme/repair) will silently skip animation because the flag is still false, causing `computeCameraFit`-based fits to jump instantly forever after the first drag.
existing_code:
// 阻止画布平移
        (sigma.getCamera() as unknown as { animated?: boolean }).animated = false;
